and sends the device the host’s information, its capabilities and the Mac’s facts: its active keyboard layout and its Mission Control shortcuts, so the device’s Bluetooth path types and gestures the same way when the helper is not running.

A session joins in warm standby. The device opens every link it can, so the helper streams nothing until the device asks for video on the link it shows. While any paired device is connected, the capture and the encoder session stay up, so video resumes with one keyframe; the encoder is fed nothing while no session takes the stream (
). With no device connected, the helper captures nothing.
The device asks for one of three kinds of video:
Full
: the full-quality stream.
Standby
: nothing is sent, and the capture keeps running.
Backup
: a second, low-rate stream at no more than 30 fps, scaled down on the GPU from the same capture, for switching links without a gap.
Every keyframe goes with the HEVC parameter sets. A device with more than two messages it has not taken yet has its next delta dropped and waits for a keyframe, because a queue of frames is latency.
If the hardware encoder stops returning frames, the stream moves to the software encoder, and the hardware is tested again while devices stay connected. If the capture stops on its own,

rebuilds it at once on a cue such as the Mac waking, and otherwise after a fixed 2 seconds, for as long as a device wants the stream. If the pipeline cannot start, as when a capture gives no first frame, it waits 5 seconds, doubling to a minute with each start that fails in a row, until a first frame. Screen Recording taken away is not retried; the permission check brings the stream back.
A session’s input goes from the network to the input lane and is posted on
’s own serial queue, in the order the device sent it, without the main actor. Each session has its own
, so the buttons and keys one device holds down are released when that device leaves, never when another does.

A device pings at least once a second on every link it keeps. After 2 seconds without hearing it, the helper stops sending it video, and resumes from a keyframe once it is heard again. After 30 seconds the session is closed and everything it held is released.

When a session ends, for whatever reason, the coordinator releases what that device held, cancels its calibration, drops its extended display request and refreshes what the pipeline runs for the sessions still open.
